note: Both sets capture the key textual values (KP(θ=0°)=0.01882681 s, KI(θ=0°)=0.008068634, KD=0.0 s², ζφ=0.7) and read the three curves of Figure 7-4. Set B is cleaner: it gives correct end-of-range reads at ~23° (proportional 0.004 s, integral 0.002, gain-correction 0.2) and only three claims at 25°, which lies beyond the plotted x-range (data ends near 23°). Set A repeats nearly every fact two or three times under two different entity names and asserts seven claims at 25° or over a 0–25° range that the figure does not support (e.g. Proportional Gain 0.005 s at 25°, Gain-Correction Factor 0.2 at 25°). A does add the useful decreasing-trend facts for all three curves, which B omits, but states them redundantly and partly with the wrong range.
remarks: The x-axis of Figure 7-4 runs 0 to about 23° (ticks 0/5/10/15/20, curves end at the right frame edge); any claim conditioned on 25° is unsupported. Both sets omit important page content: the gain-scheduling law GK(θ)=1/(1+θ/θK) (Eq. 7-20), the KI relation (Eq. 7-19), the implementation note that the previous time step's blade-pitch angle is used to compute GK at the next step, and the stated limitation that this scheduling law cannot keep ωφn and ζφ constant. Both sets use legend/axis labels as quotes for figure-derived numbers, which identifies the series but does not literally support the numeric value; this is a mild, shared weakness. Minor graph reads (0.020 s vs 0.0188, 0.007–0.008 at 0°) were treated as within reading tolerance; B's 'gain-correction factor 0.2 at 20°' is a genuine misread (curve is ~0.25 at 20°) and duplicates its correct 0.2 at 23° claim.
